answer: Biometric uniqueness makes each extra identity pay one in-person iris scan at an orb station; a farm running N fakes pays N×one real person's trip and cannot share it because an iris code belongs to exactly one living eye and cannot be transferred. The cipher registry stores only a hash of each iris, and a farm cloning one scan across a dune of 500 seats dies by uniqueness check at 2: the second enrolment matches an existing code and both seats void. One body, one code, one seat: a basalt rule, so a farm that brings no bodies earns no seats.
